> Desktop synth with three 555 oscillators, each with a pitch knob and mute switch and a mixer so we can blend the voices, a Master volume, a small amplifier and a built in speaker. A Play button along with a continuous drone mode along with a printed enclosure.  (Cover image is AI btw)

## Design

### 2026-10-20 – October 20th

**11h**

October 20th

To build a desktop synth, I divided my work into 3 different phases, the first phase is the PCB phase, then it's CAD phase, and finally the Refinement phase.

First I began with planning the circuit, I established the signal flow of three 555 oscillators feed individual level controls, a mixer, and a speaker amplifier. Also planned the battery power and play/drone controls.
![01-architecture](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/1c7d11643d8708837551df08a01a9d3b3eb3ff3aa08f610367a591cd8650091d.png)

I then started designing the first voice, I created one complete 55 oscillator circuit with adjustable pitch, a mute switch, and an output-level control
![02-single-voice](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/f2b8f781a68c7609f9617cb1a64141ab72efaab83d70fef249a9842102d88ed9.png)

I later added all three voices, by repeating the oscillator circuit to create three independently adjustable voices that can be mixed together.
![03-three-voice-schematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/b4b6bccac22ed5e7f92f6a6dff1bb5f9ebf773ede14ac313cb68bee801f83452.png)

Next I added the power and playback controls, apparently for this one I needed a battery-polarity protection, supply filtering. But I also had the PLAY and DRONE controls that enabled the oscillators.
![04-power-play-drone](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/db70b66924d6a858589f0d0d1407a44cc8a4059bdf3ed79f93fc75d43da38454.png)

I continued by designing the speaker amplifier, I added the master volume control, LM386 amplifier, output capacitor, and supporting components to drive an external speaker.
![05-speaker-amplifier](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/ff55986690a168d2d053e84b21f0b79cbfd090e9da4393aff92664e7f7b6981c.png)

Then I I had to use the KiCad Rules Checker, and the Schematic passed with 0 errors and 0 warnings. At this point I was done with the schematic.
![06-erc-zero-violations](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/5355a408aed0844f23213a1efbc22ccbc8942336009bacb6e5ce7499fb2ffbb2.png)

I later arranged the through hole components and control headers on a 100x100mm board, with 4 mounting holes for the future enclosure when I complete phase 2.
![07-pcb-placement](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/5e5e5a5171a08166afed195bd2a65100766882b1d4b05ffaf508c211d2f3b565.png)

-Short break-

Next I routed the PCB by connecting the component pads using copper traces on both sides of the board. The completed routing had 0 unconnected pads.
![08-complete-routing](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/fe4f220c8c7615eecb987c72e498eeebf732d147ef2505a0feff3958fa8d2f20.png)

Then I inspected the power, mixer, and speaker amplifier area in detail and refined the silkscreen labels to avoid overlaps.
![09-amplifier-routing-detail](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/11d343ca2a599eeb2d7f88d18d8d81823b4e19cf0ce6d8c20716f4eb2f57410b.png)

Then I ran the KiCad Design rules checker to check layout against manufacturing rules. The board passed with 0 errors, 0 warnings, and 0 unconnected pads.
![10-drc-zero-violations](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/ca0cf65c3109bfb44e822c06df319a733db18db2d2603195774f12b4caac16ce.png)

Finally I took a look at the board in 3d, to view the finished PCB with component models to review the layout and prepare a reference for Phase 2 enclosure design.
![11-pcb-3d-view](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/b73ebf80bbc98e66861e7cdbf216185e792590d9dc8137ad4f79cc4b26e8c60c.png)

P.S. This entry doesn't include information of me researching how to do this project and best things to use because I forgot to take screenshots.

### 2026-10-21 – October 21st

**10h**

October 21st

I started with the enclosure footprint and reserved space for the 100mmx100mm PCB, controls, speaker and battery. This helped me decide a layout before adding the case features.
![01-footprint-layout](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/84d84b34aeb5eb0f0f0dfc849fc7f3af16cc3defe50bce9ae399034447e5489d.jpg)

I next created the base by building the hollow enclosure with 2.4mm walls and floor, then rounded the outside corners. The open top gives access for installing and wiring the electronics
![02-hollow-base](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/450ebd6ca10ce547fa3721e5161485862359428eecc82ee5b238254c05392929.jpg)

I then needed to add supports so I created 4 mounting posts aligned to the board's 92 mm hole spacing. And then blind screw pilot holes keep the screw paths above the bottom surface.
![03-pcb-standoffs](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/6dcb1ef1f19dad9a108cfaaf6742bcc4e591e1894a63597f1867111436aecf75.jpg)

I then created internal mounting features. I added the battery rails and stops, cable tie slots, and 4 corner pillars for securing the lid. The top view shows the placement around the PCB space. The rear cradle corners received a small joining repair during final mesh validation.
![04-battery-cradle-lid-pillars](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/de1e8430d0a8086a909580bd70d300c04c45d11e4b314a1ed924477036b1a2bf.jpg)

I next had to open the case for controls, so I cut the front Play Button and Drone switch holes, and the right side power switch hole. The sizes are provisional until the exact controls were selected.
![05-front-side-control-holes](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/608fa44b2149ee928e4d857eb8c156e66176e0ef822b7928be1300e58d3d615d.jpg)

Then I had to lay out the panel, so I created the lid and placed openings for 3 pitch pots, 3 level pots, and 2 mute switches, master volume, and the 4 lid screws.
![06-lid-control-layout](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/a022814168c4f5c0b0a3ac6e8c3bb272e0ae5acd99646a892126e3516e52be76.jpg)

I later got inspirations for this next idea from my PC, where it had speaker grills, and I decided to incorporate that into the lid. I also modeled the underside speaker guides, so measurement was key here, screw bosses, and a separate retaining bridge, those underside features aren't visible, but I will show them in the Reel.
![07-speaker-grille](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/eace6de07c4eae569b02b6ee8c37348ccad79746cb4bc8919c13cf8cba7d05d6.jpg)

Next I planned to label stuff, so I recessed the project name, and control labels into the lid. During the final refinement I made the lettering bolder to improve its chances of printing clearly.
![08-engraved-control-panel](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/d463b0194cf72d76d61d4147839c34abba6e4a55d1168fa4464622ef45359ee8.jpg)

I then checked the internal layout, so I imported the actual Phase 1 PCB STEP model, corrected its position, and checked its placement inside the base. Simplified controls, speaker, and battery show the intended packaging. Those purchased part models still need confirmation against real supplier dimensions.
![09-internal-pcb-fit](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/805af25bb68f6292c9a78f5cd06b0b58c292254a26fee8415eaced598983196d.jpg)

Finally I assembled the teal base with he cream panel with provisional black controls and an orange PLAY button. I then checked feature health, checked printed part intersections against the available models, and exported the native Fusion design, STEP assembly, and 3 STL parts.
![10-complete-enclosure](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/b2e33f50edb728d49f2140c9801b937582a4c0716205dd446fe2c268e62b8ac9.jpg)

### 2026-10-24 – October 24th

**12h**

October 24th

This is  now Phase 3, where I add new features and enhance my overall workflow, so my first change was finger grip knobs, so I replaced the 7 smooth placeholder knobs with editable printable knob design having 18 finger scallops, a provisional 6.2mm shaft bore, and a M3 set screw pilot. I had to make sure base geometry was unchanged.
![01-finger-grip-knobs](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/d3385338a36bc03634f34f074b711e782921d92647923ac2444ac1aa5dd2f65d.png)

Next plan was to work on Knob Pointers, I id it on one knob which was reused a lot, so it updated all 7 instances together. The point was so that the setting can be read against the panel scales.
![02-knob-position-pointers](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/217270be01b648e9126d240388cf2cd36227b5d9ef14381d8d1b5473a2a0ad9c.png)

Next plan was to add Pitch scales, by adding 11 engraved tick marks, 0, 5, 10 labels around each pitch knob. I had to move the title and voices headings to visibly view the scales though.
![03-numbered-pitch-scales](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/180e499872b99b954ed53d876c16b7e65bdb853bf28a9e0b66ecfa0920b6ae85.png)

Next was to add volume scales, I added matching scales around the 3 voice level knobs and master volume. These are relative settings, not calibrated frequencies or decibels (because it really doesn't matter).
![04-volume-scales](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/4e0d651eb86a67472f89ac596642c8935ea94fe4b57468c7549c48aa61dbc23c.png)

Next I added voice groups, so I engraved 3 open bottom borders to group each voice's pitch, level, and mute controls.
![05-voice-grouping-borders](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/d0b8d51a1ce68ad2b2293f4961a5c300cea19c618776e722378064ee986754aa.png)

I next created mute positions, by adding an ON above each mute toggle, opposite the existing MUTE labels. Final switch orientation and wiring must match the labels during assembly. ( a note to be added to the GitHub)
![06-on-and-mute-labels](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/0ac41977af37f2432565b72db0175a293561157892525cd261d528ac5eb21dd3.png)

Next was to create external labels, I engraved the PLAY and DRONE on the front wall, and POWER on the right wall beside their existing mounting holes.
![07-play-drone-power-labels](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/7bf68015a8e8b8b28395da49fb7eb67df9ad167f25ab9c5fe0508526ca1496bb.png)

Next I added recessed lid screws, by adding four 6.4mm diameter, and 1.5mm deep screw head pockets. Flush mounting requires suitably low profile screwheads, the ordinary pan heads may protrude.
![08-recessed-lid-screw-heads](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/6a301db44ae243ff829cc60bfa41ce448c28d116f3b6b4138b2dc02e95977e24.png)

Next I wanted to work on wiring, so I added wire routing clips, by adding three C-shaped retaining clips along the left interior wall. This view hides the electronics so the clips are visible. They keep the intended wire path beside the PCB.
![09-internal-wire-routing-clips](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/a1f95c59839512f0655ad1cb0c7c1896211e9c1c09b8fd13dd46ad406b3351ba.png)

The next step was the Battery pull tab, so I added a shallow ribbon channel beneath the battery and a separate printed grip with a matching ribbon slot, the orange grip and cream ribbon ref are shown about the battery. Ribbon material might have to be bought.
![10-battery-pull-tab](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/57892e11d73a52935fab1d6b951a5cf08192abb5caed19e4e42dd57ca3bcb99e.png)

Next I made rubber foot pockets, by recessing four 12.4 mm diameter seats into the underside for nominal 12mm adhesive feet. Pocket depth is 0.6mm.
![11-rubber-foot-pockets](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/8d6501180bc0521c98415e0515b79441f3644517dce700f1184c325420527089.png)

Next I made a speaker grill, I replaced the circular perforations with 7 rounded slots within the same speaker area. The nominal webs are 1.4mm wide. I did this for a better design
![12-improved-speaker-grille](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/f01f7e84a24b4d5004edee79b77ba1fc6bc84700e6255cd340c41658dcaa9455.png)
